title: Peel police officers given Medals of Bravery for stopping armed man at Brampton courthouse
subtitle: Const. Mike Klarenbeek and Const. Dave Lakha recognized at Rideau Hall
article: Two Peel Regional Police officers who stopped a gunman from entering a Brampton courthouse in 2014 were awarded medals of bravery this week.
Governor General David Johnston presented Const. Mike Klarenbeek and Const. Dave Lakha with the awards at a ceremony in Rideau Hall on Friday.
"Together, the officers brought down the gunman and prevented further tragedy," said a press release from the event.
Johnston addressed all of the award recipients at the ceremony.
"Instead of playing it safe, which is a natural instinct, protective, you faced danger head-on. And we're much safer and better off for it," he said.
"You simply acted with no regard for your own personal safety, and with only one driving force: to protect someone else."
On March 28, 2014, a man named Charanjit Singh Bassi entered the A. Grenville and William Davis Courthouse in Bramton and tried to go through security line reserved for staff and lawyers.

A Special Investigations Unit report said that one of the officers, who police identified as Klarebeek, told Bassi to join the public line. Bassi then pulled out a pistol and fired two shots at Klarenbeek, one of which hit him in the torso.
In the resulting chaos, Bassi went through the security checkpoint where he was confronted by another officer and the two fired at each other.
By that time, Klarenbeek had gotten back on his feet and shot three times at Bassi, killing him.
Johnston presented 41 Medals of Bravery and two Stars of Courage at the ceremony on Friday.
